preamble: Rhotacization of the alveolar implosive: [ɗ] becomes [r]. Gravina (2014) reports a regular change *ɗ > r in Bura (Margi group), and a word-final *ɗ > r in the Higi-group languages Kamwe (Nkafa), Kirya and Bana, where *l > r also took place. Elsewhere in Central Chadic *ɗ is usually kept, reduced to [ʔ], or lost. An implosive alveolar stop has a short closure, so it is easily reinterpreted as a tap or trill, as also happens with plain intervocalic d.

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 51), example (22): a regular change in Bura.
